supporting_observations.claim: At 13:38 UTC, the domain controller issued a service ticket for paul.becker to the WS-DREYES-01$ service from client IP 10.52.10.23. This is close in time to the reported PowerShell window, but the record does not establish a successful interactive or remote PowerShell session.

At 13:40:48 UTC, WS-DREYES-01 made a proxy request to download.windowsupdate.com using the Windows Update Agent; the proxy returned status 502. This is compatible with, but does not prove, the scheduled workstation patching activity.
At 13:42 UTC, WS-DREYES-01 requested Kerberos tickets for FILE-COP-01$ using its machine account. The records do not show what resource or process used those tickets.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not include a process-creation event identifying PowerShell, its parent process, command line, or user at the reported time.
The supplied records do not show whether the patch script was read from FILE-COP-01 or whether a remote PowerShell session was established.
The administrator service-ticket record does not by itself establish that paul.becker successfully logged on to WS-DREYES-01 or performed the reported activity.
claims_not_established: Whether the reported PowerShell window was caused by authorized workstation patching or by another activity.
Whether the 13:38 service ticket and the 13:40 report are part of the same activity.
What commands, if any, ran in the reported PowerShell window, and whether they caused changes or network activity.
additional_evidence_needed: Collect endpoint process and PowerShell logs for WS-DREYES-01 around 13:40 UTC, including process creation, parent process, command line, script-block logging, and user context.
Review remote logon and PowerShell remoting evidence on WS-DREYES-01 and WS-PBECKER-01, including successful logons and session details.
Check FILE-COP-01 file-access or share-audit logs for access to \\FILE-COP-01\IT\Patch-Workstations.ps1 and correlate it with the administrator activity.
Confirm with IT whether paul.becker initiated patching on WS-DREYES-01 at that time and whether the activity matches the approved procedure.
unrelated_findings: Dropbox.exe was launched on WS-DREYES-01 under dan.reyes; Dropbox is a file-sharing service not listed as approved. Route this for separate review; it does not establish anything about the reported PowerShell window. (T104-00071, T104-00072, T104-00073)
